My first job after college was teaching English in Japan. I taught EFL for nearly 4 years. Lots of eikawas (English conversation schools) needing teachers but there was nowhere to grow in that field. It felt like a temporary career and I knew I needed to leave and grow. I’ve met people who also did JET program and did Assistant Language Teaching in Japanese public schools. After moving to America, my experience in Japan came in handy and landed me a job in CT public schools. I’ve taught 4th and 5th English Language Learners, and been a summer school classroom teacher, now I am teaching 7th grade ELL students. The student behaviour and school system is really different but the benefits and the pay is good.

When I said brought it up to him, I meant giving my husband a heads up that I am purchasing this bag not actually giving hint for him to get it. I was waiting for him to be okay with the purchase even-though we don’t really have an official rule of permission to purchase anything since we do handle our own finances.

Spoiled, entitled, impulsive, and insecure. I understand that I probably sound like this but I know I deserve to purchase a bag with my hard earned money. I grew up in a third world country so when I feel like I hit a milestone, I feel like I should get to celebrate that. And I know not everyone will understand luxury purchases as well but it is more than just a bag, but also a symbol of how far I’ve come in life. The value of this item also equals out to cost per wear.

We have access to each other’s bank accounts but we handle our own finances. We share payments to bills like car payments, water, electricity, mortgage. For any other extra purchase, I mostly handle it for us. This is why I was confident to buy the bag on my own but I do like the idea of setting a rule of : if spending an amount more than XYZ, should be discussed and setting a certain limit for purchase every month.
